BEHIND THE GREAT FACE — the gallery directly behind the giant translucent clock-face, colossal brass gears meshing against the glowing amber dial, the reversed hands sweeping slowly across it.
TOWERING GEAR HALL — a cathedral-huge hall of stacked interlocking brass cog-wheels rising into shadow, driveshafts and bevel-gears threading between them, iron catwalks clinging to the frame.
PENDULUM WELL — a deep vertical well where the great brass pendulum swings its slow arc, the escapement ticking above, catwalks ringing the shaft into the gloom below.
MAINSPRING CHAMBER — the vast coiled mainspring fills one iron-walled room, its tension singing through the frame, the anchor escapement rocking its slow measured beat against the ratchet wheel.
BELL CHAMBER — high above the works the great bronze bells hang in their timber frame, iron clappers poised, the strike-train gears below them wound tight against the next hour.

BEVEL-GEAR SHAFT — a vertical shaft lined with interlocking bevel-gears and driveshafts transmitting torque upward, each meshing pair gleaming with oil, the whole column trembling faintly with mechanical life.
BRASS CATWALK GALLERY — a narrow brass catwalk threads between colossal cog-wheels, handrails vibrating with each mesh, the teeth of enormous gears passing inches away in their ponderous rotation.
INNER WORKS FROM BELOW — looking upward from the base, tier upon tier of gears recede into shadow, driveshafts crossing the void, the whole mechanism framed by iron beams above.
THE GREAT WHEEL CHAMBER — the primary great wheel dominates the room, its brass teeth the size of a man's forearm, the pinion it drives spinning fast against its slow sweep.
ESCAPEMENT GALLERY — the anchor escapement rocks its precise beat at the heart of the hall, pallets clicking against the escape wheel's teeth, the entire gear train held to its rhythm.
FUSEE CHAMBER — the conical fusee rotates against the mainspring chain, equalising the drive through its spiral flanks, housed in a low iron vault dense with the smell of clock oil.
INTERMEDIATE GEAR TRAIN HALL — a long hall where the intermediate gear train steps up from slow to fast, each successive pinion smaller, the final shaft spinning in an almost invisible blur.
STRIKE TRAIN VAULT — the strike train's count wheel and locking plate govern the blow sequence, gears clicking through their detents in the low vaulted chamber, the lifting pieces already rising.
WINDING SHAFT GALLERY — great winding shafts descend through the floor on iron bearings, ratchet clicks echoing off the brick walls as the weights are drawn upward against the next day's running.
DIAL-WORK CABINET — the dial-work motion train reduces the minute shaft to hour, its three small wheels and two pinions ticking in a brass cabinet mounted directly against the stone rear face.
GREAT PENDULUM FROM THE BRIDGE — from the iron bridge spanning the pendulum well, the bob passes below in a slow majestic arc, the rod flexing almost imperceptibly at each reversal.
UPPER GEAR HALL — at the tower's upper tier the gear hall narrows but heightens, cog-wheels smaller and faster here, their teeth a bright blur, the brass framework trembling with accumulated speed.
OIL-CISTERN LEVEL — below the main works a maintenance level holds oil cisterns and drip-trays, the undersides of great wheel hubs visible overhead, slow drops falling from pivot holes into pans.
FOURTH-WHEEL LANDING — the landing at fourth-wheel height, where the gear train has stepped the rotation to near-second pace, the wheel's teeth strobing past the fixed index plate in the lamplight.
WEIGHT-PIT — far below the works the massive iron driving-weights hang on their lines over the pit floor, their slow descent the stored energy that drives every gear in the tower above.
CLOCK-FACE ANNEX — a side annex where the motion-work connects through the stone wall to the external dial, the squared shaft turning in its bearing, a faint amber glow leaking through the joint.

CROSSBAR LANDING — a broad iron crossbar landing bisects the gear hall mid-height, gears passing through slots cut to accommodate them, the whole structure vibrating as the great wheel train meshes around it.
GOVERNOR CHAMBER — a centrifugal governor spins in its own iron chamber regulating the strike train's speed, its brass balls rising and falling on their arms, the collar governing the warn wheel.

FRAME GALLERY — the great seat-board frames of the clock stand exposed from the gallery level, the pivot holes precisely drilled through seasoned iron, every arbor visible end-on in its polished bearing.

RATCHET VAULT — a low vaulted room holds the great maintaining-power ratchet, its click-spring pressing firm against the teeth, keeping the train alive during winding, the detent arm gleaming with oil.
BELL LOFT — the great bronze bells hang in the open-timbered crown of the tower, their clappers rigged to iron rods descending into the works below, the air still resonating.
WORKS FROM BELOW — looking upward from the pit, tier upon tier of brass gears recede into shadow, driveshafts crossing the vault overhead, the entire mechanism a luminous iron sky.

DIAL GALLERY — the curved gallery directly behind the clock-face, great cannon-pinions driving the hour and minute tubes, the frosted glass glowing amber with daylight filtered through the painted dial.
GREAT WHEEL CHAMBER — the massive great wheel, tallest in the going-train, turns its slow revolution here, each brass tooth the size of a forearm, the drum cable groaning under load.
COUNT WHEEL ALCOVE — the slotted count wheel governs the strike sequence in a low vaulted alcove, iron pins tripping the detent, the mechanism clicking through its measured cycle in the dark.

FLY GOVERNOR GALLERY — a pair of iron fly-governors spin furiously on their vertical spindles, limiting the strike train's speed, their paddles blurring in the lantern-lit recess between the frame plates.
LOWER SUMP LEVEL — below the pendulum well's foot, an oil-floored sump catches drip from the great train above, iron support columns descending into it, the pendulum's arc ending just overhead.

STRIKING TRAIN CHAMBER — the striking train occupies its own iron-framed chamber beside the going-train, a deeper, heavier smell of grease here, the great count-wheel turning its slow circuit between strokes.

ESCAPEMENT PLATFORM — a narrow iron platform surrounds the anchor escapement, the pallets rocking in their steady rhythm, each impulse face catching the escape-wheel tooth and releasing it with a sharp tick.

MOTION WORK GALLERY — the motion work fills this low gallery between the dial and the great wheel, cannon-pinion, minute-wheel and hour-wheel turning in their fixed ratios, barely a handspan of clearance overhead.

INTERMEDIATE WHEEL PASSAGE — a narrow passage where intermediate wheels of the going-train bridge the frame, their arbors running in polished brass bushings, the entire passage trembling with low continuous mechanical frequency.
HAMMER LEVER HALL — long iron hammer-levers pivot on their arbors above the bell loft stairs, tails resting on the pin-barrel below, lifting and releasing to drive the clappers against the bronze.

PIN-BARREL CHAMBER — the massive cylindrical pin-barrel rotates on its horizontal arbor, iron pins projecting from its surface in the pattern of the chime melody, lifting each hammer-tail in sequence.
CLOCK TOWER CROWN — at the very crown of the works, driveshafts terminate in the bell-frame, wind entering through open louvres, the bells ranked by size above the final bevel-gear coupling.
WINDING GALLERY — the winding squares project through the front plate here, the great winding keys socketed onto them, the ratchet clicks echoing through the gear hall as the weights are raised.

FRAME PLATE PASSAGE — the narrow gap between the clock's massive front and back plates, arbors and pinions occupying every inch, the hum of the going-train conducted through the iron into one's palms.

PENDULUM SUSPENSION CHAMBER — directly above the pendulum well, the suspension spring and crutch occupy a vaulted recess, the crutch fork embracing the pendulum rod, each swing nudging it with the escapement's impulse.
GREAT WHEEL GALLERY — the chamber housing the primary great wheel, a brass ring taller than three men, its pinion engaging the next wheel in a chain of slow, unstoppable force.

INTERMEDIATE GEAR DECK — a mid-tower platform where intermediate wheels of graduated brass mesh in ranked rows, their arbors socketed into iron plates, the whole assembly humming with transferred motion.
ESCAPEMENT BRIDGE — an arched iron bridge spanning the gear hall, directly above the escape wheel, the anchor pallet-arms rocking in steady beats, each tick releasing one tooth with a click.
CALENDAR WORK ALCOVE — a vaulted recess beside the main train where the calendar mechanism stacks its slow wheels, a month-wheel advancing by one tooth each midnight through the silent works.

STRIKING TRAIN GALLERY — a side gallery housing the striking train's count-wheel and lifting-pieces, iron detents engaging their notches, the mechanism counting out each hour in deliberate, locked sequence.
GREAT PENDULUM CROSSING — the catwalk level where the pendulum rod sweeps through its broadest arc, the brass-and-iron rod nearly grazing the ironwork, the air displaced in a slow rhythmic wave.

OIL-LANTERN WALK — a maintenance catwalk circling the gear hall's mid-level, iron oil-lanterns mounted at each major arbor, their amber light pooling across the faces of slowly revolving brass wheels.

CROWN-WHEEL CHAMBER — a vaulted cell housing an older crown-wheel escapement preserved within the mechanism, its upright teeth engaging a verge foliot, a relic of an earlier clock embedded in the works.
WEIGHT-SHAFT PIT — a deep square pit below the gear hall where the drive-weights descend on iron cables, the pit walls worn bright by decades of the cables' slow, inexorable travel.

MOTION-WORK CABINET — a recessed iron cabinet behind the dial where the motion-work multiplies wheel-turns to drive the minute and hour pipes, small polished brass gears spinning faster than the main train.
GREAT DRUM GALLERY — the floor housing the great rope-drum from which the driving weight is suspended, its iron flanges grooved by cables, slowly unwinding its circumference across each passing day.
UPPER BELFRY APPROACH — the final iron stair ascending past the last gear cluster into the bell chamber, the floor vibrating with each bell-strike, the air dense with brass resonance.
RACK-AND-SNAIL ALCOVE — a side recess where the rack falls against the snail cam to count the hours, iron rack-teeth engaging precisely, the tail dropping to its notch with mechanical certainty.

GOING-TRAIN VAULT — the central vaulted chamber of the going train, five great wheels in linear sequence from mainspring to escapement, each arbor socketed in polished brass bushings set in the iron frame.

LANTERN-PINION GALLERY — a dim gallery where older lantern-pinions of iron rod and brass disc mesh against great wheels, the cylindrical cages turning silently, a mechanical forest of rotating brass columns.
BACKPLATE GALLERY — the narrow walkway behind the mechanism's great backplate, the reverse faces of all the wheel-cocks and cock-screws exposed, the plate itself a dense engraved continent of brass.

DRIVESHAFT VERTICAL SHAFT — a narrow vertical passage packed with spinning driveshafts and bevel-gears, each meshing the next, torque cascading upward through grease-dark iron into the mechanism above.
BRASS-CATWALK GALLERY — a narrow brass catwalk threading between colossal cog-wheels, their teeth passing inches from the railing, the floor vibrating underfoot, oil mist hanging in the amber light.
LOWER WORKS LOOKING UP — from the base of the mechanism, gears recede upward through stacked floors of ironwork, shafts vanishing into shadow, the whole interior alive with measured turning.

INTERMEDIATE GEAR TRAIN — a long horizontal run of intermediate gears stepping down the mainspring's force, each brass wheel enormous, their axles seated in polished iron pillow-blocks, perfectly aligned.
FLYWHEEL RECESS — a deep alcove housing the governing flywheel, its arms spinning in a blur of brass, regulating the power flowing through the gear train beyond the iron partition.

CLOCK-FACE ANNULUS GALLERY — a circular gallery running the full circumference of the clock-face frame, colossal brass cannon-pinions driving the hands above, the glowing dial curving around the walkway.
WEIGHT SHAFT — the long vertical shaft through which the driving weights descend on their iron cables, the walls close on either side, the cables bar-taut in the half-dark.
PILLAR FRAME INTERIOR — within the clock's iron pillar frame, the platework rising in tiers, each plate pierced for axle-arbors, the whole interior ordered and precise as a brass instrument.
LANTERN PINION ROW — a run of brass lantern pinions meshing with great contrate wheels along one wall, the cylinder-rod teeth catching the light, the row extending deep into the gear hall.
MOTION WORKS GALLERY — the gallery of motion works behind the dial, cannon pinions and minute wheels turning in their ordered sequence, the glowing face throwing amber light across the brass.
BELL-STRIKE TRAIN CHAMBER — the strike train's dedicated chamber, its count wheel stepping around, the hammer-tail cams ranged on their shaft, each one ready to lift and release its hammer.
SUSPENSION SPRING ALCOVE — the pendulum's suspension spring hangs in its narrow alcove above the well, the thin brass ribbon flexing with each arc, the crutch engaging the anchor above.
GOING TRAIN PASSAGE — a narrow passage beside the going train, the wheel-teeth passing at eye level, each gear's rotation slowing the next in the long reduction down to the hands.
IRON PILLAR BASE — at the base of the iron pillar frame, the floor plates are thick with grease and wear, the lowest great wheels turning just above, their axles plunging deep.

QUARTER-CHIME CHAMBER — the quarter-chime mechanism fills this chamber, its pin-barrel studded with brass pins, the hammer-arms ranked above, the great bells of the quarter sequence hung beyond the partition.

GREAT-WHEEL CHAMBER — the first-wheel barrel occupies the chamber's center, its enormous brass great-wheel engaging the pinion train, chain-lines vanishing upward into the mainspring housing overhead.
MINUTE-TRAIN GALLERY — a horizontal gallery where the minute-train gears spin at perceptible speed, their polished brass faces catching amber light from the dial beyond the iron bulkhead.
HOUR-WHEEL RECESS — a recessed alcove where the slow hour-wheel and its cannon-pinion turn barely perceptibly, thick brass spokes furred with verdigris, their motion measurable only by patience.
COUNT-WHEEL VAULT — a vaulted side-chamber housing the great iron count-wheel, its notched periphery advancing one click per hour-stroke, the hoop-wheel pivoting on a polished steel arbor.
WINDING-SHAFT ALCOVE — the square winding-shaft descends through the floor, its iron ratchet-work and click-springs arrayed around it, the weight-lines running over polished brass pulleys overhead.
WEIGHT-DROP SHAFT — a deep shaft through which the massive iron driving-weights descend on braided-wire lines, their slow fall powering the entire train, catwalks crossing the abyss on iron brackets.

INTERMEDIATE GEAR HALL — a mid-tower gear hall where intermediate-train wheels of diminishing diameter mesh in sequence, the whole array humming with transferred energy, iron pillars bracing each wheel-arbor.
FLY-GOVERNOR CHAMBER — the fly-fan governor spins on its vertical arbor in a vaulted side-bay, its brass vanes blurring, governing the chiming train against runaway acceleration.
CANNON-PINION PLATFORM — the cannon-pinion and its concentric motion-work occupy the platform behind the dial, minute and hour pipes turning on their common axis against the glowing clock-face.
STRIKING-TRAIN GALLERY — a long gallery housing the striking-train wheels, count-levers, and warning-wheel in sequence, their interaction releasing the bell hammers above at each counted hour.
LOWER FRAME HALL — the massive cast-iron seat-board and lower frame fill the hall, great pivot-holes bushed in brass, the entire wheel-train supported on precisely bored iron plates.
LANTERN-PINION RECESS — a narrow recess where early lantern-pinions of rolled-iron staves mesh with a colossal crown-wheel, the primitive geometry of old horology preserved within the modern train.

UPPER BEVEL-GEAR CROSSING — a junction platform where bevel-gears redirect rotational force through ninety degrees, driveshafts branching left and right toward the bell-hammers and the dial-drive simultaneously.
PENDULUM-SUSPENSION BRIDGE — the narrow iron bridge spanning the pendulum well at mid-height, the great pendulum rod passing through its slotted center at each slow swing, air moving with it.

CLOCK-FACE ANNEX GALLERY — a wide gallery flanking the rear of the clock-face, colossal cannon-pinion motion-work turning against the amber glow, the great reversed numerals readable through the translucent opal dial.

INTERMEDIATE GEAR GALLERY — a mid-level gallery where intermediate reduction gears step down the mainspring's force, brass pinions and steel wheels meshing in long trained sequences across the iron floor.
STRIKING TRAIN ALCOVE — a side chamber packed with the striking train's count-wheel and detent, iron levers pivoting in sequence, releasing the bell hammers on their precisely measured schedule.
SECOND FACE GALLERY — behind the tower's second clock-face, a duplicate arrangement of brass motion-works presses the reversed hands across the glowing opal dial in the amber afternoon light.
FLYWHEEL CHAMBER — the heavy brass flywheel of the chiming train spins on its arbor, smoothing the impulse of the released spring into the even rotation the count-wheel demands.
GREAT PENDULUM BASE — at the bottom of the pendulum well, the bob's polished brass lens sweeps back and forth at floor level, its slow tick felt more in the chest than heard.
IRON FRAME INTERIOR — deep inside the main plate-frame, the pivot holes of a dozen arbors align in precision rows, each brass wheel spinning true on its polished steel pivots.
CHIME BARREL ROOM — a pinned cylinder barrel as wide as a cartwheel turns slowly, each pin lifting a hammer lever in sequence, programming the chime melody into the waiting bronze bells.
UPPER DRIVESHAFT COLLAR — where the main vertical driveshaft passes through an upper floor collar, bevel gears divert power laterally into the gear hall's outer reaches with a deep mechanical groan.

CATWALL JUNCTION — two brass catwalks intersect between the flanks of opposing cog-wheels, the crossing platform vibrating with transmitted gear-mesh forces, oil droplets tracing arcs through the amber-lit air.
LOWER GEAR HALL — the lowest register of the gear hall, where the slowest and largest wheels turn, their teeth barely perceptibly moving, yet driving all the urgency of the works above.
NIGHT FACE GALLERY — the clock-face gallery in darkness, the dial glowing faintly from outside gas-lamps, the great gear-teeth flashing amber and shadow as they press against the luminous glass.
RATCHET AND CLICK CHAMBER — a compact iron chamber housing the maintaining ratchet and click spring, holding the great wheel while the clock is wound, teeth locked against the pawl's iron shoulder.
GREAT BELL STRIKE PLATFORM — the platform from which the great hour-bell's hammer arm pivots, a massive iron lever balanced on its fulcrum, waiting for the count-wheel to release its blow.

MAINTAINING-POWER RECESS — a recessed alcove housing the maintaining-power spring and detent, small precision gears gleaming against blackened iron, the click of the ratchet marking each swing of the pendulum.

MOTION-WORK GALLERY — the narrow gallery behind the dial where motion-work gearing converts the going-train's rotation to hand movement, brass cannon-pinions and minute-wheels turning in close-fitted iron brackets.
FLYWHEEL VAULT — a low vaulted chamber where the heavy iron flywheel spins on its horizontal arbor, its mass steadying the strike-train, brass oil-cups gleaming at each bearing housing.
GOING-TRAIN BRIDGE — an arched iron bridge spanning the gear hall, the going-train's wheel-stack mounted along its length, each pivot running in jewelled brass cocks bolted to the bridge-plate.

STRIKE-TRAIN LOFT — the loft where the count-wheel and pin-barrel of the strike-train govern the bell sequence, iron levers and lifting-pieces arranged in mechanical ranks above the going-train below.
FOURTH-WHEEL PLATFORM — the iron platform where the fourth wheel drives the seconds hand arbor, the wheel's brass teeth a bright blur, its pivot steady in the polished brass cock above.
BARREL ROOM — the deep chamber housing the great going-barrel, its ratchet-click echoing off stone walls, the click-spring glinting as the click rides each tooth of the great iron ratchet-wheel.

ESCAPEMENT RECESS — the alcove where the recoil anchor pivots above the escape wheel, its pallets catching and releasing each tooth in sequence, the escapement's tick resonating through the iron frame.

INTERMEDIATE GEAR PASSAGE — a low iron-vaulted passage packed with intermediate reduction gearing, colossal brass wheels meshing with small steel pinions, the gear hall's noise concentrated here to a deep mechanical roar.

UPPER CATWALK RING — the uppermost catwalk ringing the gear hall just below the bell chamber floor, colossal crown-wheels turning at eye level, the bronze bells' hanging chains descending through holes in the planking.

BEVEL-GEAR JUNCTION — a junction chamber where four driveshafts meet through meshing bevel-gears on a central iron cross-frame, each shaft departing to a different level, brass collars and set-screws at every hub.

WINDING-MECHANISM GALLERY — the gallery housing the weight-winding gear, a heavy iron ratchet mechanism engaging the drum as the counterweight descends, the click of the pawl steady and deliberate in the stone space.
GREAT PENDULUM BOB LEVEL — the mid-shaft catwalk at the level of the great pendulum's brass bob, the bob sweeping past at arm's reach, its slow momentum pressing a faint wind against the ironwork.

FRONT-PLATE CHAMBER — the chamber between the clock's front and back plates, the full depth of the going-train visible between polished brass plates, wheel-arbors ranked in their pivot-holes across the dim interior.

OIL-SINK INSPECTION WALK — the low inspection walkway where oil-sinks at every pivot can be reached, small brass cups set into the cock-plates, the gear hall's vast noise reduced to a steady iron resonance.

TOWER BASE MACHINERY FLOOR — the stone-flagged floor of the tower's base where the great weight-lines descend from above, iron pulleys and guide-frames bolted to the walls, the pendulum well dropping away through the center.
